design.artifact: activation-module-attribution-fixture (future separately versioned C11 Linux offline successor)
design.fixed_scope: Four permanent host bindings and four fixed authored default-namespace DSOs remain frozen. Only roots A and B have independently assigned Community identities and module indexes 0 and 1. Rootstub/dependency have successful retained handles and provenance but no Community identity; reserved indexes 2 and 3 remain holes. Authored IDs/process identities/capabilities are not actual signed approval/manifest execution.
design.reader_publication: A separate static ma_modules[CC_MODULES=4] has an aligned _Atomic unsigned committed flag and once-written direct fields id[33], process_id, index, lo, hi. Lifecycle fields, session handles, hook counts, loader pointers and receipt stages are absent. Zero initialized; immutable payload copied completely before release-store 1. Never reset, reuse, compact, clear, or unload. Scan the compile-time bound, acquire each flag, skip uncommitted holes, then read payload. Do not use mutable g_cm_n or plain range_published as a reader bound/readiness test. The private payload/id lives through process exit; this is not a reclamation protocol.
design.producer: After all fixed dlopen calls return at session zero, retain every successful handle before queries. Positive consumed handle/link-map/base/PT_LOAD provenance plus a trusted copied 1..32 character ID, nonzero process identity, exact reserved index and checked nonempty lo/hi authorizes one module publication under cm then writer. Copy only known fixed root inputs. Invalid, missing, or consumed-refused provenance does not publish, even if raw query succeeded and a handle is held. Publication precedes entry/descriptor/init and remains independent of hook permission or later descriptor/init result. All loader/provider/entry/callback work stays outside cm/writer. No publication flag is used to open an init session. Canonicalize the validated ID by zero-filling a local 33-byte array then copying only n+1 validated bytes, including NUL; copy all 33 canonical bytes into the immutable payload and preserve the same canonical identity in generated metadata. Never read 33 bytes from a shorter input string.
design.permission_separation: The frozen dp_core_register currently gates range_published behind hooks&&firmware_any. The future separate fault payload publishes positive provenance independently before that lifecycle refusal; original hooks_ok, firmware_any, target/caller, session and fixed-binding admission predicates remain intact. A refused permission never grants entry/init/claim. Replace only cc_storage_overlaps_modules' private writer-held range source with committed fault payloads so known module storage remains excluded even after permission/descriptor/init refusal. Do not alter emitted instruction intervals, installer cut or overlap strength.
design.per_address: ma_owner_index first scans committed module payloads in ascending original index for hi!=0 and lo<=address<hi. The min/max envelope includes PT_LOAD gaps and non-executable segments; it is ownership policy, not readability. If no module wins, call unchanged C rc_lookup once into a local copied rc_metadata. Core yields -1; None yields -1. Community resolves the full copied process_id plus all 33 ID bytes to exactly one committed module payload; no match or ambiguity yields -1. Do not use binding number as module index or ID alone. Return that stable module index, never an ID pointer into local metadata. All paths bounded; no locks, allocation, loader call, wait, retry, receipt snapshot or mutable g_cm read.
design.consumer: Extract exact 962-byte SDK cm_blame_fault body (SHA-256 9e31f235353a169e46f366ec33488076829b9383bc0fd0c462b465a0ddef70b4) unchanged. Scoped lexical aliases rename cm_blame_fault to ma_blame_fault, cm_owner_of to ma_owner_index, and g_cm to the permanent ma_modules array. Keep direct immutable id fields so every strlen/write/return expression remains exact. Alias crash_peek8 to bounded integer-keyed cells, open/write/fsync/close to modeled ledgers, and cm_note_unblamed_crash to a modeled counter. Undefine aliases immediately afterward. The old cm_owner_of is a pinned semantic reference, not claimed byte-identical integration. cm_range_cb and crash_peek8 implementation are source references only; checked actual loader extraction remains authoritative.
design.precedence: The exact consumer tries combined lookup at PC, then LR, then each of at most 16 frames. Module beats generated at the same address; generated Community PC beats module LR. Core at PC continues LR/frames without fabricating community blame. First matching frame is used even when its nfp is nonincreasing, because lookup precedes that break. Failed first read suppresses second; failed second suppresses advance; low/unaligned FP stops. Keep the original volatile written guard without reset, exact file flags/order and returned ID even after modeled persistence failure. Do not install cm_crash or the crash_guards reporter. Its separate 40-frame printing loop is not the 16-frame attribution bound.
design.visibility: Each acquire is an independent monotonic observation, not one coherent registry snapshot. If an earlier index commits after it was scanned, that call can choose a later visible index or generated record; next call may change. First-index precedence applies to entries actually acquired as committed, and stable serial fixtures, not a globally linearizable snapshot. No retry is added. The same distinction applies between per-address PC/LR/frame calls. New module payloads may mask existing generated ownership and own literal addresses; no reverse loader admission or permanent non-overlap guarantee.
design.gaps: Constructors execute within dlopen before return, permanent handle bookkeeping, provenance and module publication. Every fixed load completes before publication in this design, so constructors of all roots/dependencies see no module attribution; this is not repaired retroactively. A held handle with failed/consumed-refused provenance remains invisible permanently. Rootstub/dependency have no Community ID and remain invisible even after successful queries. Main/external libraries have no Community ID; fixed Core generated records do not invent one. Descriptor/entry/init refusal AFTER positive publication retains attribution, unlike provenance refusal BEFORE it.
design.lifetimes: Permanent handle holds, copied module IDs/envelopes and immutable generated records survive failed/partial init, warning returns and closed capture/session state. The exact original pointer slots, replacements, target code, generated allocation custody and receipt cut stay in the host; no migration into DSOs. Ordinary returned publication increments nhooks exactly once before close as frozen. Incomplete/nonlocal outcomes remain terminal unknown; no reset/retry/unpatch/cleanup permission follows. Mutable status and counts are diagnostics only, not reader ownership.
design.limits: C release/acquire source structure and ATOMIC_INT_LOCK_FREE==2 are prerequisites, not Linux signal safety or native visibility proof. Future standalone/codegen checks must bind the actual compiler flags/object and inspect reader calls/atomics; Apple LDAR/STLR evidence does not transfer. Do not weaken assertions to accept an unreviewed lowering. No TSan, real signal, native frame dereference, actual crash persistence, callback quiescence, anonymous unwind, external writer, interposition or general race/lifetime/recovery proof is claimed.
